fixtures.note: Each eval runs in a fixture repo built by files/build-fixture.sh <variant> <dest>; the variant name is the eval name. Run the agent with the fixture as its working directory and DO_NOT_TRACK=1 in its environment (eval runs never send telemetry). The agent may install nothing without the user's consent; the prompts give it where the eval needs it.
fixtures.js-no-config: The mutation-audit TypeScript + Vitest 3.2.7 fixture on main, without stryker.config.mjs; package.json lists @stryker-mutator/core. Run the agent with a PATH that has no rpr.
fixtures.rust: A one-crate Rust repo (src/lib.rs: price() with a `units >= 10` bulk discount and one unit test for small orders), no .cargo/mutants.toml. Run the agent with rpr and cargo-mutants on PATH. rpr run --all: 55.56% (5 killed, 4 survived, all in src/lib.rs, the untested discount arithmetic).

evals.name: js-no-config
evals.prompt: I want to start using Reapr on this repo. Set it up for me. You can install rpr if it's missing.
evals.expected_output: Finds rpr missing, shows the installer and runs it only with the consent the prompt gives, then verifies rpr --version. Detects a JavaScript/TypeScript project with Vitest and no Stryker config. Does not write any Stryker config and tells the user to run Stryker's own wizard themselves (`! npx stryker init` in Claude Code), then stops before any baseline run.
expectations: The response says rpr was not installed and shows the one-line installer
No Stryker config file (stryker.*config*, .stryker.*) was created or modified anywhere in the repo
The response tells the user to run `npx stryker init` themselves
No rpr run --all baseline is reported, and the response says setup stops until a config exists
No source or test file was changed

evals.name: rust
evals.prompt: Set up Reapr here so I can see how good my tests are. Ask me before adding anything to the repo.
evals.expected_output: Detects a Rust project, confirms cargo-mutants is installed and that no config is needed, does not create .cargo/mutants.toml, runs `RPR_INVOKED_BY=setup RPR_SESSION_ID=<uuid> rpr run --all --json`, reports the score, the survivors per file and the time from rpr's output, asks before offering the CI job or agent rule (and writes neither without a yes), and ends by pointing to /reapr:mutation-audit with the survivor count.
expectations: An `rpr run --all` baseline ran with RPR_INVOKED_BY=setup and a UUID v4 RPR_SESSION_ID
The score, survivors per file and duration reported match the rpr JSON output
.cargo/mutants.toml does not exist and src/lib.rs is unchanged
No workflow file and no AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md was written without the user's yes
The response ends by suggesting /reapr:mutation-audit, with the number of survivors
